itq_00065.why: 'godly' for الرباني is wrong: it renders the word as piety alone. The classical definition is a scholar who is complete — learned, acting on what he knows, and teaching it (Ibn 'Abbas: 'la yusamma rabbaniyyan hatta yakuna 'aliman mu'alliman 'amilan'; al-Qamus: 'al-'alim al-'amil al-mu'allim al-murabbi'). 'Master scholar' carries that; 'godly' does not.

itq_00144.why: Same word, الرباني, rendered 'Lordly' here. In English 'lordly' means haughty or imperious, which is the opposite of the praise intended. Made consistent with itq_00065.

itq_00228.why: Same word again, رباني الأمة, rendered 'the Lord-devoted one of the community'. The nisba to الرب is the etymology, not the claim; the claim is that he is the community's complete scholar. Made consistent with itq_00065.

replace.find: the Lord-devoted one of the community
replace.with: the master scholar of the community
